Disclosure to Promote the Right To Information 

Whereas the Parliament of India has set out to provide a practical regime of right to 
information for citizens to secure access to information under the control of public authorities, 
in order to promote transparency and accountability in the working of every public authority, 
and whereas the attached publication of the Bureau of Indian Standards is of particular interest 
to the public, particularly disadvantaged communities and those engaged in the pursuit of 
education and knowledge, the attached public safety standard is made available to promote the 
timely dissemination of this information in an accurate manner to the public. 




Mazdoor Kisan Shakti Sangathan 
"The Right to Information, The Right to Live''

UDC 685-635-7 { First Reprint MAY 1989 ) IS : 5460 - 1969 



Indian Standard 

SPECIFICATION FOR 

SOFT BALLS 



( Reaffirmed 2000 ) 



[In preparing this standard, rules and regulations of the game accepted internationally have 
been adhered to while giving consideration to the manufacturing and testing practices prevalent in the 
country and abroad. Any change occurring in these rules and regulations will immediately be taken 
care of by this Sectional Committee in consultation with the national controlling body of the game in 
the country. ] 

1. Scope — Dimensions and requirements of soft balls. 

2. Material 

2.1 Core — 85 to 113 g of compressed long fibre Indian kapok [soft, smooth, clean, dry, reasonably 
free from seeds and other extraneous matter and silky in appearance (see IS : 3040-1965') ], hand or 
machine wrappv d with fine quality twisted yarn and covered with latex or rut]ber cement, 

2.2 Cover — Tight-textured cowhide leather, free from flay cuts and grain defects, semi-chrome 
tanned or chrome tanned, natural or dyed in any colour as agreed to between the purchaser and the 
manufacturer. However, at the end of tanning operation and before drying, suitable fungicides shall 
be incorporated into the leather and these shall be effective and non-toxic. Further, the tanned 
leather shall be sub3t::ntially fat-liquored and grain finished smooth. The pieces of leather used 
for construction shall be such as will stretch uniformly, so as to avoid the ball losing shape in 
usage. 

3. Shape and Dimensions — As shown in Fig. 1. 




Circumference 302 to 308 mm 

Weight 170 to 191 g 

FIG. 1 SOFT BALL 



4. Construction and Workmanship — Core shall be obtained by wrapping tightly by hand or machine 
the already compressed long fibre Indian kapok with fine quality twisted yarn and thereafter covering 
it with latex or rubber cement. The two sections of the cover shall be cemented to the core by 
application of cement to the underside cover and sewn with waxed cotton or linen thread. The 
sections shall be well stitched and the stitches shall be well stretched out. The thread used for 
stitching shall be strong enough to withstand the normal usage. The finished ball shall be substan- 
tially regular, round, smooth seamed, of concealed stitch or flat surfaced. The construction shall not 
give rise to outseam balls which. are excluded under the rules. 



*Specification for Indian kapok for stuffing purposes. 



Adopted 22 December 1969

5. Marking — To be marked with the following: 

a) Manufacturer's name or initials, or recognized trade-mark; and 

b) The words *Made in India'. 

5.1 Certification Marking — Details available with the Bureau of Indian i,^andards. 

6. Packing ™- Each bail shall be wrapped in moisture-proof paper, and packed in cardboard boxes or 
as agreed to between the purchaser and the manufacturer. 



Reprography Unit, BIS, New Delhi, India
